newsitem.title: USA: Medfly quarantine extended to Florida county.
newsitem.headline: Medfly quarantine extended to Florida county.

text.p: The Agriculture Department said it added a portion of Florida's Hillsborough County to the list of quarantined areas to prevent the spread of the Mediterranean fruit fly, a highly destructive pest.

In a notice published in the Federal Register, the agency's Animal and Plant Health Inspection Service said it was also adding home-grown eggplant to the existing list of regulated products under quarantine for the Medfly.
The interim rule became effective on Monday, the agency said.
The Medfly can cause huge losses of fruits and vegetables. Recent trapping surveys by Florida inspectors showed an infestation of the Medfly in a part of Hillsborough County, near Tampa.

The USDA also said it proposed to add home-grown eggplant to the list of products regulated for the Medfly after determining that fully ripe eggplant can host the pest. The agency said that commercially-produced eggplant is harvested at a stage of development when susceptibility to Medfly infestation is unlikely.
